title: Whitespace-only title or author
description: The source rejects empty values and is silent on whitespace-only input. Options: treat whitespace-only as empty, or accept it. Treating it as empty is the narrowest reading of a reader-facing 'empty'.

title: Response contract for rejected submissions
description: The source gives no status code or error channel. Chosen: POST /books returns 400 with a JSON error body; the HTML form route re-renders the page with status 400 and a visible message.

title: Response for removal
description: The source gives no removal response contract. Chosen: DELETE /books/{book_id} returns 204 on success and 404 for an unknown id.

title: Browser form routes versus JSON API
description: Browser forms cannot issue DELETE, so the screen provides POST /add and POST /remove/{book_id} over the same services as the JSON routes. Server-rendered HTML with no client-side JavaScript was chosen as the narrowest interface.

options.label: Client-side fetch against the JSON API

title: Validation error message format
description: Missing, non-string, or whitespace-only fields produce 'title must be non-empty text' (or 'title and author must be non-empty text' when both fail). This names the field and is human-readable, as the spec requires. Acceptable, or should the wording change on replan?

title: How bin/test.sh behavior is tested
description: The runner tests copy the real bin/test.sh into a temporary application root and run it with a stub pytest first on PATH. Running the real script from inside pytest would recurse. Is that acceptable?
